gameLoopReview.evidence: The live loop is mechanically deep and well instrumented, but grenade lethality bypasses the shared defeat lifecycle and live movement duplicates its extracted contract. Empirical retention remains unscored beyond design judgment because production funnel and participant evidence are absent.
prioritizedFindings: A grenade can reduce an enemy to lethal health without awarding/removing it through the score, combo, loot, achievement, boss, and cleanup lifecycle; rail and projectile paths duplicate that lifecycle with observable drift.
Keyboard, touch, and gamepad movement are recomposed inline even though a tested pure movement contract already exists, leaving the extracted contract disconnected from live play.
The coverage headline excludes the systems and hooks that own most pure gameplay/runtime contracts, so the aggregate is narrower than its label implies.

Route live keyboard, touch, and gamepad movement through one tested frame contract.
Publish and enforce an explicit core-logic coverage scope with measured ratchets.

items.title: Make every lethal damage source enter one exactly-once enemy-defeat lifecycle instead of letting grenade kills bypass rewards and cleanup.
items.why: The grenade step only subtracts health and writes lastDmgSource. Rail and projectile collision own separate ~150-line defeat branches, while enemy movement continues after grenade processing. This can leave grenade-lethal enemies alive in the simulation until an unrelated projectile collision and makes combo, score, loot, boss, sound, split, and achievement semantics drift by damage source.
items.recipe: Extract a source-neutral defeat transition with an idempotent enemy marker and one App-level effect executor. Route grenade, rail, and projectile lethality through it in the frame they occur; preserve source-specific precision/beat metadata outside the common lifecycle. Add parity fixtures for standard, boss, splitter, nemesis, grenade, rail, projectile, and duplicate-finalization cases, plus a static architecture guard that prevents new per-source defeat branches.

L1.recipe: Finalize and remove grenade-lethal enemies immediately with focused regression coverage.

L2.recipe: Share score/combo/coin/stat transitions across grenade, rail, and projectile kills while preserving source-specific effects.

L3.recipe: Build the exactly-once source-neutral lifecycle, converge all defeat side effects, cover boss/split/loot/achievement parity, and add a regrowth guard.

items.title: Connect the live keyboard, touch, and gamepad path to one pure movement-frame contract instead of maintaining a dead extraction beside inline runtime logic.
items.why: systems/gameStep.js exports and tests computeMovementVector/applyPlayerMovement, but App.jsx recomputes keyboard, touch, gamepad composition, normalization, speed modifiers, clamping, and obstacle push-out inline. The testable contract therefore does not prove the path players actually use, and gamepad is absent from the helper signature.
items.recipe: Extend the pure input contract to combine keyboard, touch joystick, and gamepad vectors with finite-value sanitation and stable normalization. Wire App.jsx to the contract for all ordinary movement, retain dash ownership, and emit the existing debug source receipt from the same resolved frame. Cover simultaneous-source cancellation, analog bounds, rubble/adrenaline modifiers, canvas clamps, obstacle centers, keyboard-only, touch-only, and gamepad-only parity.

L1.recipe: Call the existing helper for keyboard/touch while leaving gamepad addition inline.

L2.recipe: Extend and wire one three-source movement vector with focused parity tests.

L3.recipe: Add sanitized multimodal composition, live integration, source receipts, pathological-input fixtures, and architecture assertions.

items.title: Turn coverage from an unlabeled subset headline into an explicit, source-derived core-logic contract with fail-closed ratchets.
items.why: test:coverage reports one All files aggregate, but vite.config.js includes only src/utils, storage.js, and constants.js. src/systems and src/hooks contain the pure gameplay, integrity, damage, progression, and frame contracts yet are absent from the coverage scope, so the headline can improve while critical logic regresses unmeasured.
items.recipe: Create one importable coverage contract defining included surfaces, honest exclusions with rationale, minimum file count, and measured statement/branch/function/line floors. Consume it from Vitest, emit json-summary, and validate the summary after each coverage run. Expand scope to systems/hooks, add focused tests for newly exposed high-value gaps rather than lowering floors, and make the validator fail when scope, file count, or metrics silently shrink.

L1.recipe: Expand include patterns to systems/hooks and add a JSON summary.

L2.recipe: Centralize scope/floors and validate the measured summary after test:coverage.

L3.recipe: Add fail-closed scope/file-count/metric ratchets, explicit exclusions, regression tests for the validator, and close the most important exposed gaps.
